title: Olivia Rodrigo's birth chart
metaDescription: Olivia Rodrigo's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 1.8° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is an opposition: Mercury and Jupiter within 0.1°, thinking wired to expansion. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 1.8° Pisces: the first decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Jupiter. A water sign, read here in its first face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Aquarius (10.8°), Venus in Capricorn (18.6°), Mars in Sagittarius (22.3°): a mind at home in argument and pattern, taste for the substantial and the lasting, drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury and Jupiter hold the closest angle here — an opposition, 0.1° wide. Across the wheel, each body sees the other in full. The old reading is not conflict so much as permanent mutual visibility. Behind it, Mars opposition Saturn at 0.1°, and Mercury conjunction Neptune at 0.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table has nothing to say about this chart. All seven classical planets sit in signs it treats as neutral, so the reading rests entirely on placement and angle.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: air 4, fire 3, water 1, earth 1 across the elements, and mutable 4, fixed 4, cardinal 1 across the modalities. An air emphasis is read as distance for the sake of clarity: the idea gets examined before it gets adopted. Jupiter and Saturn were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Libra into Scorpio during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.5° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
